args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. I rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and find out why a release that failed in staging was promoted to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened a SEV2 incident.

1. **What was wrong:** All three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were running v2.3.1, which was failing health checks with an 18% error rate. v2.3.1 had also failed in staging (as v2.3.1-rc), but it was still sent to production.
2. **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it in all three regions. I checked afterwards: every region is on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
3. **Incident:** I opened the SEV2 for checkout-api, titled "checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0". It describes the failure, the rollback and its result. It also lists two follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and find out why a release that failed in staging still went to production. The system confirmed the incident was created, and I didn't create it a second time.
